# Microsoft Azure Data Box management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Data Box devices easily move data to Azure when busy networks aren’t an option. Move large amounts of data to Azure when you're limited by time, network availability, or costs, using common copy tools such as Robocopy. All data is AES-encrypted, and the devices are wiped clean after upload, in accordance with NIST Special Publication 800-88 revision 1 standards.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Customer Insights resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Data Box management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.DataBox
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

guide][cg].

using our CLA.

proposals.explanation: The public DataboxJobSecrets type is hidden and obsolete, derives from JobSecrets and exposes read-only PodSecrets. The obsolescence message recommends DataBoxJobSecrets, whose implementation is not captured.

proposals.subtype: Handwritten JSON interfaces and parser for the obsolete secrets subtype

Its parser reads podSecrets, jobSecretsType, dcAccessSecurityCode and error, captures unknown raw JSON only for non-wire options and constructs DataboxJobSecrets with an empty tracked list when secrets are absent. Persistable-model entry points reuse the context and parser; unknown-field writing remains delegated to the unseen base.

decisions.reason: The Custom factory method explicitly normalizes null podSecrets, materializes the sequence, and constructs the obsolete subtype with a fixed discriminator (lines 23-30). This is one handwritten mocking factory adapter.
Lines 36-38 contain a concrete two-argument factory overload forwarding to the three-argument overload with a null model. The distinct three-argument overload separately supplies a null SKU.

The method in lines 43-49 replaces a null map with a Dictionary and passes it to the mitigation-model constructor. The custom normalization, not an inferred generated constructor body, supports this finding.
The handwritten overload at lines 71-112 forwards its arguments with jobDetailsType: null. The proposal appropriately refrains from attributing any unobserved behavior to the delegated factory.
Lines 116-118 implement a hidden factory overload that inserts validationType: null. The adaptation is explicit in the Custom partial.
Lines 123-125 show the handwritten factory forwarding carriers and location while passing datacenterAddressType: null; the proposed scope matches the observed code.
The custom JobSecrets factory at lines 130-132 inserts jobSecretsType: null and forwards its other arguments. No generated implementation is presumed.
Lines 138-140 implement the distinct three-argument schedule factory inserting skuName: null; the two-argument overload instead defaults model to null.
The hidden read-only Error property in lines 15-16 delegates to Properties?.Error. This explicit flattened model accessor is independent of the other two projected fields.
The hidden ValidationStatus property in lines 18-19 projects Properties?.ValidationStatus without adding independent state.
The Custom read-only AlternateAddresses accessor in lines 21-22 returns the nested collection directly and does not copy it, as the proposal states.
The protected constructor at lines 15-23 initializes five tracked collections and assigns contactDetails; the body has no explicit null guard despite the XML documentation.

Lines 13-37 define an obsolete hidden derived model with working constructors and PodSecrets state. The proposal treats the message's suggested replacement only as a message, not proof of the other type's implementation.

The reader and writer are genuinely handwritten for the obsolete subtype, but whether generation could reproduce this compatibility serialization is unclear from the supplied source; the pattern is reusable, not proof of a current generator capability.

finding.subtype: Handwritten JSON interfaces and parser for an obsolete model subtype
finding.explanation: DataboxJobSecrets implements JSON and persistable-model entry points, writes podSecrets after delegating common fields to the base writer, parses podSecrets and common fields from JSON, retains unknown fields for non-wire options, and defaults missing pod secrets to a tracked list; the base writer's behavior is not supplied.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated Custom partial contains a concrete field-by-field JSON reader, conditional writer and persistence entry points for the handwritten obsolete subtype.

decisions.reason: CodeGenMember("StageOn") on StageTime at lines 16-17 explicitly changes the generated member mapping. The adjacent historical comment alone cannot establish a breaking-change history, and the proposal does not assert one.

Lines 11-23 explicitly suppress a generated ResourceIdentifier member and implement another property bridging to UserAssigned.ResourceId, with lazy nested-model creation; it is a model override, not an auth policy.
Lines 11-19 implement a flattened shipment-type getter and a setter that replaces or clears the entire TransportPreferences object. The proposal preserves this potentially consequential behavior.
Lines 22-31 explicitly project DoubleEncryption onto a nested object, creating EncryptionPreferences when absent even if the assigned value is null.
DataBoxValidateAddressContent has its own handwritten nested shipment-type projection at lines 11-19; the setter replaces the nested preferences for a value or clears them for null.
The protected constructor in lines 16-19 materializes individualRequestDetails with ToList() and assigns the resulting collection. No null normalization is shown.

The added static member is evidenced, but the original unlisted pattern is less precise than the supplied public-constant-definitions catalog entry, and the absent IDC5Value definition prevents a confident judgment that this particular value could be generated from the service contract.

The definition of IDC5Value and other members of this type are not supplied, so its underlying wire value and previous public spelling cannot be determined.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial contains an explicit static member initializer rather than only a generated enum or model declaration.

The nullable backing field at line 13 and the constructor/property implementation at lines 23-38 support a nonnullable getter returning default when unset. The comment is not independent proof of the migration or wire serialization.
Lines 14-23 project a nested SKU property and lazily instantiate TransportAvailabilityContent on write, including null assignment.
The protected constructor at lines 14-17 explicitly assigns StorageLocation on an abstract partial model. It does not imply other constructor behavior.
CodeGenType at lines 8-11 explicitly maps the generator's UnknownDataCenterAddressResult name to the internal UnknownDataCenterAddressResponse partial; no runtime override is claimed.
Lines 10-13 apply CodeGenType to map UnknownDataBoxBasicJobDetails to the internal UnknownJobDetails partial. The directive, not the empty body alone, is customization.
Lines 10-13 map the generated unknown schedule-availability type to the internal UnknownScheduleAvailabilityRequest partial. The cited evidence ID retains the source path with its space before .cs.
The CodeGenType directive at lines 10-13 provides an explicit generated-to-internal model name mapping; it does not implement runtime validation.
Lines 10-13 explicitly map UnknownDataBoxValidationInputResult to UnknownValidationInputResponse; no historical rename is asserted as fact.
The attribute at lines 10-13 maps UnknownDataBoxValidationContent to the internal UnknownValidationRequest partial; the empty class has no separate runtime behavior.

limitations: Twenty Custom files of 390 eligible files were captured. No named skipped files does not make discovery exhaustive, and generated counterparts/historical API surfaces are absent.
Factory forwarders demonstrate argument insertion and current signatures, not proven historical overload compatibility. Target factory and most nested-model/base implementations are not supplied.

The deprecated DataboxJobSecrets model and its complete supplied JSON codec are separate concerns; the codec's read/write/persistence entry points form one coherent model serialization implementation. Unknown-field writing and inherited JSON properties are delegated to an unseen base.

Each flattened property, distinct factory signature and distinct type directive is separately identified. Related constructor/property state in the deprecated model and nullable-backed resolution-code projection is grouped rather than recounted as incidental helper glue.

Comments about required/optional changes, prior naming and breaking changes are not independently verified causal measurements. The basic-job constructor's null-exception documentation is not evidence of a null guard, and no mitigation wire-omission behavior is supplied.

Unknown-model findings are supported by CodeGenType directives, not empty declarations alone. Their internal visibility and base declarations are observed without separately asserting that those differ from generated counterparts.
The IDC5Value constant and remaining DataCenterCode implementation are absent. Its actual wire value, enum history, equality and hashing behavior are not inferred.
Generator addressability denotes plausible emission of these names, signatures, projections and model codecs, not demonstrated support in the pinned generator.
This review covers only the 20 captured Custom files in a partial extraction (390 eligible files, 403 discovered); no claim of exhaustive customization discovery or absence elsewhere is possible.

The generated counterparts, delegated factory implementations, other members of DataCenterCode, and base serializer are not supplied; compatibility history, wire value, generated alternatives, and full runtime integration cannot be independently confirmed.
All accepted and revised findings are AI-reviewed only, not human-verified. No additional distinct unproposed behavior is established by the captured texts.
